parameters.content:
## AI agent that rebuilds websites with MiroMiro

### How it works
A chat agent that reads and rebuilds websites. Open the chat in **Chat with the Agent** and ask, for example, "Turn the hero of linear.app into a React component" or "What are the brand colors and fonts of airbnb.com?". **Website Rebuild Agent** decides which MiroMiro tool to call: **Get Brand Kit** for colors, fonts and logo, or **Turn Section into Code** for a section (hero, header, pricing, footer...) as React, read from the live page in a real browser. It replies with the code and a preview link. If a site cannot be read, the agent says why. Failed calls are not charged.

### Setup
This template uses the verified community node **n8n-nodes-miromiro** (tested with version 0.1.4 on n8n 1.123).
1. On n8n Cloud, search "MiroMiro" in the nodes panel (an admin may need to turn on Verified Community Nodes). Self-hosted: Settings > Community nodes > Install `n8n-nodes-miromiro`, see https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/
2. Get a free MiroMiro API key (300 credits a month, no card): https://miromiro.app/api/onboarding
3. Open **Get Brand Kit** > Credential > Create new, and paste the key.
4. Select the same credential in **Turn Section into Code**.
5. Add your Anthropic credential in **Claude Chat Model**, or swap it for OpenAI, Gemini or any chat model.
6. Click **Open chat** and ask about a website.

A brand kit or a section costs 10 MiroMiro credits. The same call again within 24 hours is free.

### Customization
Change the output in **Turn Section into Code** to Tailwind, HTML, Vue, Elementor or Shopify. Add the other MiroMiro operations (images, fonts, design tokens) as more tools. Connect the agent to Slack or Telegram instead of the n8n chat.

![The workflow, in case the preview does not load](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SoraiaBarroso/n8n-nodes-miromiro/main/docs/templates/ai-agent-rebuild-websites.png)

options.systemMessage: You help people rebuild websites. Return the code exactly as the tool gives it, then add the previewUrl so they can see it rendered. If a tool returns an error, tell the user what went wrong in one sentence.
